Using a new, unique combination of hidden bidding and worker placement, players manage resources to craft various musical instruments in their workshop, while also courting actual historic patrons through an ever-changing personal tableau of actions and bonuses. Each player chooses how to balance improving skills across multiple tracks, unlocking specialized worker abilities and other bonuses. The choice to concentrate on varying gameplay strategies and goals, such as musical performances, instrument building and repairs, apprentice training and workshop expansion, and overall reputation as an instrument maker, provide multiple paths to victory. Luthier finds true harmony through an authentic and original marriage of theme and mechanisms, resulting in a rich gameplay experience that equally speaks to both the strategic gamer and the classical music lover. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Luthier is played over 6 rounds with players building and/or repairing instruments, performing, satisfying patron wishes, and claiming public goals. Contents 1 START OF GAME SETUP for each Player 2 HOW TO PLAY: 2.1 ACTION LOCATIONS: 2.1.1 Salon 2.1.2 Guild 2.1.3 Perform 2.1.4 Repair 2.1.5 Balcony 2.1.6 Roughing Bench (personal player board) 2.1.7 Finishing Bench (personal player board) 2.1.8 Marketplace (no workers required) 3 How To's: 3.1 HOW TO FINISH A PATRON: 3.2 HOW TO RESET A PATRON'S PATIENCE CUBE (cube under a Patron): 3.3 HOW TO GET LIRA (money) 3.4 HOW TO GET RESOURCES (resource cubes) 3.5 HOW TO GET INSPIRATION (! tokens) 3.6 HOW TO GET PRESTIGE POINTS (victory points) 4 END GAME START OF GAME SETUP for each Player - Choose a family which provides things like starting resources, lira (money), apprentices, Inspiration (!), and potentially an extra worker and other starting benefits. - The number on the family also determines the starting player order. - Choose a Patron from the 2 cards dealt to you. - Choose an Instrument from the 2 cards dealt to you - Choose 2 Private Goals from the 4 cards dealt to you Suggestion: Choose Private Goals that align with Public goals (above the game board), if possible. See if any public or private goals are for Patrons or Instruments and choose accordingly. Choose a starting instrument that your Patron requires. HOW TO PLAY: Start of Each Round: - Patron Patience Cubes are advanced and bonuses are collected. If a Patience Cube advances to its last position, the Patron is removed and the player is docked 3 Prestige Points (victory points). - Up to 2 instruments may be placed on the player's Roughing Bench, as space is available. Planning Phase: - Each player starts with a minimum of three workers (round tokens marked 1, 3, 5, unless a family benefit grants more), which are used to "bid" on which actions the player would like to do in that round. - Workers (and any accompanying apprentices) are placed one at a time, in turn order, in action locations the player would like to do that round. Resolution Phase: - Once all players have placed their workers, in turn order, players choose an action location, in which they have a worker, to resolve. Worker tokens are placed in order first by value and any ties are resolved by first placement to last placement order. The player with the highest worker (+apprentice) value takes their actions first at that location, then the next, down to the lowest number. - When all players with workers on that action location have finished, the next player in game turn order (shown in the Balcony) selects the next action location to resolve. [Rating: 2/10] Right in the zeitgeist for over-designed games. Could have been great if it wasn't so deliberately convoluted.

[Rating: 2/10] Worst of this kind of game I've ever played.   Everything depends on which cards come up when, and if the cards available to you don't work together,  you are fucked.  The actual gameplay isn't fun or interesting enough to overcome is fatal flaws.

[Rating: 2/10] Luthier board game notes  Second Play *updated* with a worse rating  This game is too random, doesn’t not contain interesting mechanics and has poor end game scoring.  People are too focused on the art and components to realize this is a poorly designed game. The game is too long with 4 players at 3 hours. Bidding bidding mechanic is interesting but doesn’t do much for the game or theme.  2 games we’ve played and repair crafting is underwhelming.  The game would be better without making 2 tiers of crafting.  Don’t play this game. There are many far better euro games.

[Rating: 3/10] In this above average euro weight game, players are going to try to gain the most points after 6 rounds. On a players turn, players add a new instrument into the left side of their board, then in turn order place workers (valued 1-5) on any worker space (any number of workers can be on one space). Once that's complete, players will (in turn order) activate 1 location at a time, starting with the player with the highest numbered value to the lowest, ties broken by who placed there first.
